messages:
marta (devex): Heads up, QA hit intermittent SSL failures with the python SDK on Windows inside CI venvs. Only on our corporate runners. error: `certificate verify failed`. anyone have quick triage steps?

ryan (qa): repro on Win2019 hosted runner, python 3.9.13. Locally on dev boxes works. In CI: `ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED]` when contacting api.redwood.com.

luca (sdk): common causes: cert bundle mismatch (certifi vs Windows store), corporate TLS inspection, or pip wheel/cryptography mismatches. quick checks: `python -c \"import ssl, certifi; print(ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION, certifi.where())\"` and `python -c \"import requests;print(requests.utils.default_ssl_context())\"`

alex (windows): on Windows the distinction is Schannel vs OpenSSL. CPython builds on our runners use OpenSSL and rely on bundled certs. If the corporate root isn't in that bundle you'll see failures. For build agents that use system CA, venvs can still miss corp roots.

marta (devex): tried `pip install --upgrade certifi` in the venv on the runner, still failed. Any env vars we should try?

luca (sdk): try `set SSL_CERT_FILE=%(python -c \"import certifi; print(certifi.where())\")%` (PowerShell/Windows syntax adjust) or set `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` to your pem that includes the corporate CA. You can also pass `verify='/path/to/chain.pem'` to requests at runtime.

ryan (qa): setting REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE to the corp chain fixed CI in one run but flaky elsewhere. The chain is large (7 MB) and seems to cause timeouts sometimes.

alex (windows): timeouts could be from TLS handshake renegotiation with certain cipher suites. Check OpenSSL version: older 1.1.1 builds have different defaults. `python -c \"import ssl; print(ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION)\"`

marta (devex): on the flaky runner it's OpenSSL 1.1.1k. On a stable runner it's OpenSSL 3.0.0.

luca (sdk): another SDK-side mitigation: expose a Client(ca_bundle=...) parameter so callers can pass explicit chain path rather than env var hacks. Also we should improve the error message when verification fails to include: OpenSSL version, certifi path, and a hint about corporate MITM. I'll open an issue.

sam (docs): I'll add a short troubleshooting section in quickstart titled "Windows CI venv TLS errors" with commands + examples for setting REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and SSL_CERT_FILE.

ci-bot: Created issue rwin/py-sdk#655 - "Add ca_bundle parameter to Client and improve TLS failure diagnostics" (assigned to luca)

luca (sdk): assigned. Plan: short-term add better logging and README note. medium-term add `ca_bundle` arg and an env var `REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE` that overrides requests verify path. Need to sync with security about ship-time defaults.

ryan (qa): one more datapoint: when we switched CI from venv to system site packages (no isolation) the failures disappeared. Seems like certs are injected into system store but not into venv's certifi bundle. Not ideal but helps triage.

alex (windows): note: some AV products intercept and provide a local cert which only shows up in the Windows cert store, not in certifi. For corp-managed runners, the right move is to ensure the runner image's certifi bundle includes the corporate CA or set SSL_CERT_FILE globally for the runner.

marta (devex): thanks. ryan can you paste the runner images and python versions in the issue? we'll prioritize fixes in SDK + docs.

ryan (qa): will do. thanks all. happy to validate any change. :thumbsup:
